newsitem.title: MEXICO: Keen to lend, Mexico banks see few reliable clients.
newsitem.headline: Keen to lend, Mexico banks see few reliable clients.

text.p: The head of Mexico's bankers' association said on Tuesday that the country's banks were ready to resume lending but were unable to find creditworthy customers.

The statement came after criticism from Mexican business leaders that Mexican banks would lend money only on the basis of guarantees and not on project viability, and that they paid scant attention to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises.

"We are only going to lend to projects that are genuinely viable, that generate cash flows, and that are managed by genuine companies," the president of the Mexican Bankers Association, Antonio Del Valle, told a conference in this northern Mexican city.
"If a company is highly indebted, though it may have the best plans in the world, we are not going to lend to it," he added.
Mexican banks have been reluctant to lend since the 1995 peso crisis when government and banking sector bailouts to cash-strapped debtors totalled some $30 billion.
Del Valle said the banking sector had decided to protect itself from the error of lending too readily, as happened in the run-up to the crisis.

While companies complain they do not have access to financing from Mexican banks, forcing them to take on dollar liabilities or issue shares, Del Valle acknowledged that lending to consumers had slowed.
Here also Mexican bankers have decided to lend money only under the strictest conditions.
